title: So the Reformed grant the gifts please God but do not precede his favour
source_text: XII. Unde patet Doctores Reformatos non negare fidem, spem, charitatem, & similia Spiritus Sancti dona esse res Deo gratas, & quarum ratione homo, in quo reperiuntur, Deo placeat & gratus sit: sed tantum ista dona non praevenire Dei favorem & benevolentiam erga nos, verum ejus esse effecta & munera.
pass_a_gloss: XII. Whence it is plain that the Reformed Doctors do not deny that faith, hope, charity, and similar gifts of the Holy Spirit are things pleasing to God, and by reason of which the man, in whom they are found, pleases God and is pleasing: but only that those gifts do not go before the favour and benevolence of God toward us, but are its effects and gifts.
pass_b_english: Thesis XII. It is clear from this that the Reformed doctors do not deny that faith, hope, love and similar gifts of the Holy Spirit are things pleasing to God, on account of which the person who has them pleases God and is acceptable to him.
They deny only that these gifts come before God's favour and goodwill toward us. Rather, they are its effects and its gifts.

lemmas.latin: non praevenire Dei favorem & benevolentiam erga nos
lemmas.gloss: do not go before the favour and benevolence of God toward us

choices.term: gratia gratis data ... gratia gratum faciens
choices.english: grace freely given ... grace that makes pleasing
choices.why: The scholastic pair (Aquinas, Summa theologiae I-II q. 111 a. 1): gifts given for the good of others versus the grace that makes its bearer pleasing to God. Kept literal because the Reformed objections turn on the very words.
